intro: Colorado mails a ballot to every active registered voter. County clerk and recorders run elections, under the Secretary of State.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and local offices, plus any measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Ballots mailed to voters
dates.detail: County clerks mail a ballot to every active registered voter. They start Oct. 2 and must be done by Oct. 9. You don't need to ask for one.

dates.label: Drop boxes open
dates.detail: Every county must have its drop boxes open by this date. The state expects 452 drop boxes. They take ballots through 7 pm on Election Day.

dates.label: In-person voting at voter centers
dates.detail: Every county must have its voter service and polling centers open by Oct. 19. The state expects 384 centers. You can vote, drop off a ballot, or get a new one there. Find sites and hours at GoVoteColorado.gov.

dates.label: Last day to register and still get a ballot by mail
dates.detail: Register or update your record at GoVoteColorado.gov by this date to get a ballot in the mail. After Oct. 26 you can still register and vote in person at a voter center, up to 7 pm on Election Day.

dates.label: Last suggested day to mail your ballot back
dates.detail: After this date, take your ballot in its signed envelope to a drop box or voter center, or vote in person. Postmarks do not count.

src.label: Colorado Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Voter centers are open 7 am to 7 pm. Your ballot must reach your county clerk by 7 pm, or you must be in line by 7 pm. Postmarks do not count.

src.label: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 election calendar (PDF)
Colorado Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs

dates.label: Last day to fix a signature problem
dates.detail: If your county clerk tells you there is a problem with the signature on your ballot envelope, you have until this date to fix it.

id_rule.text: Everyone who votes in person must show ID. Many kinds count, such as a Colorado driver's license or ID card, a U.S. passport, a military ID, a Medicare or Medicaid card, a Colorado college student ID, or a recent utility bill or bank statement (within 60 days) with your name and address. An ID that shows an address must show a Colorado address. Some first-time voters who vote by mail may need to send a copy of an ID with their ballot.
